claim: La Campana in Rome has been registered at its current address since 1518 and is run by the Tracassini family, making it among the world's oldest continuously operating restaurants.
quote: According to recently discovered tax documents, La Campana has been registered at its current location since 1518. The restaurant was originally run by Pietro della Campana, an innkeeper who paid a road maintenance tax.

claim: La Campana's official site is ristorantelacampana.com; it sits near Piazza Navona and the Pantheon and serves traditional Roman cuisine, open since 1518.
quote: La Campana is located at Vicolo della Campana, 18/20, and has been registered at the same address since 1518 ... certainly the oldest since it has been open since 1518.

claim: Antico Caffè Greco, founded in 1760 near the Spanish Steps, is Rome's oldest coffee house and hosted figures like Byron, Goethe, Keats, Casanova, Wagner and Mark Twain.
quote: Over the centuries this elegant coffee house has hosted illustrious characters such as Lord Byron, Buffalo Bill, Casanova, Goethe, Henry James, Keats, Shelley, Mark Twain and Wagner.

claim: Antico Caffè Greco has served customers since 1760, is the oldest coffee bar in Rome and second-oldest in Italy after Venice's Caffè Florian (1720).
quote: Antico Caffè Greco, a stone's throw from the Spanish Steps, has been serving customers since 1760 and is the oldest coffee bar in Rome and the second-oldest in Italy, after the Caffè Florian which opened in Venice in 1720.

claim: Buca Lapi was founded in 1880 in the cellars of Palazzo Antinori in Florence and serves Tuscan classics including bistecca alla fiorentina.
quote: Buca Lapi was established in 1880, originating 'nelle cantine di Palazzo Antinori' (in the cellars of Palazzo Antinori) ... signature dishes include ... bistecca alla fiorentina.

claim: In 1880 the Antinori family opened a trattoria in their palazzo cellar and named it Buca Lapi after their tavern keeper Orazio Lapi.
quote: In 1880, the Antinori family opened a trattoria and hired Orazio Lapi as the 'tavern keeper,' and the family decided to call the trattoria after Orazio Lapi - Buca Lapi.

claim: Antico Fattore in Florence has served Florentine and Tuscan dishes since 1865 and was a gathering place for artists including De Chirico, Morandi and Carena.
quote: Countless famous names would animate Antico Fattore's Wednesday nights, including artists like De Chirico, Morandi, and Carena.

claim: Harry's Bar in Venice, founded 1931 by Giuseppe Cipriani at Calle Vallaresso 1323 near Piazza San Marco, is an iconic Venetian rendezvous.
quote: Harry's Bar in Venice is an iconic rendezvous since 1931 ... Harry's Bar sits steps from Piazza San Marco at Calle Vallaresso 1323.

claim: Harry's Bar is the birthplace of the Bellini (1948, named for painter Giovanni Bellini) and Carpaccio (created c.1950 for Countess Amalia Nani Mocenigo, named for painter Vittore Carpaccio).
quote: Carpaccio was born in 1950, because of the particular diet of Amalia Nani Mocenigo, an Italian countess to which the doctor had prohibited cooked meat ... The red-and-ivory palette reminded him of the Renaissance painter Vittore Carpaccio.

claim: Harry's Bar was declared a National Landmark by the Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage in 2001 and counted Hemingway, Capote, Chaplin and others among its patrons.
quote: The Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage declared it a National Landmark in 2001. No other public place in Italy had received the same award in the same Century.

claim: Pizzeria Brandi in Naples, founded 1760, claims the 1889 invention of the Pizza Margherita by chef Raffaele Esposito for Queen Margherita of Savoy, its three colors mirroring the Italian flag.
quote: In 1889, chef Raffaele Esposito created the Pizza Margherita to honor 'Queen Margherita of Savoy who was visiting Naples' ... tomato (red), mozzarella (white) and basil (green).

claim: A plaque at Pizzeria Brandi in Naples marks it as the birthplace of the Pizza Margherita, unveiled in 1989 on the 100th anniversary of the dish.
quote: A plaque near the Pizzeria Brandi marks the location as the birthplace of the pizza Margherita. It was unveiled in 1989, on the 100th anniversary of its invention.
